_doc: Lift-and-shift view of every finding rule (used when assessment.json assessment_type is lift-and-shift). Question asked of each rule: when the same server image / application runs on Amazon EC2 with the same operating system, does this stop working or behave differently, and who acts on it? Rules not listed here are 'future': they matter only if the code is later modernized (Linux, .NET 10, PostgreSQL) and go to the Future options section, never into the move or the estimate. Row format: RULE: [area, owner, change, severity, action]. owner: dotnet = the application team (code and configuration); devops = servers, network, domain / identity, VM migration, CI runners; dba = databases and their server features; security; vendor = hosting or software vendor; business = the client's business owner. change: config = a configuration value changes (becomes a CI variable); code = source code must change; server = something must be installed, registered or created on the EC2 host; network = firewall, route, DNS, allow-list; identity = domain, account or directory access; decision = the client must decide or confirm; verify = nothing known breaks, check after the move. severity is the lift-and-shift severity (it replaces the modernization severity in the move sections; a reviewer's adjusted severity still wins). Only owner dotnet with change code is costed per finding; configuration changes are priced per CI variable by config_template.py + estimate_effort.py, and everything else is a hand-off to the owner.

areas.machine: Tied to the machine (hardware, name, registry, certificates, installed software)
areas.mail: Mail, file transfer and other servers
areas.integrations: Printing, reporting, Office and other on-premises integrations

NET-ENDPOINT-INTERNAL: Replace the address with a CI variable. DevOps decides whether the target moves to EC2 (new address) or stays on-premises (route over VPN / Direct Connect).
NET-ENDPOINT-PUBLIC-IP: A fixed public address in code or config. Check whether the provider allow-lists our source IP; if so, give them the new AWS Elastic IP.
NET-UNC-SHARE: The file server and share must exist on AWS (FSx for Windows or an EC2 server) or stay reachable. The .NET team changes the path in configuration.
NET-SMTP: The mail relay must be reachable from EC2. AWS blocks outbound port 25 from EC2 by default: use port 587 or ask AWS to lift the limit.
NET-FTP: The FTP / SFTP server must allow the new source IP (and passive ports). Servers keep the same address only if they stay put.
NET-PROXY: The proxy must be reachable from EC2, or the setting removed if EC2 has direct outbound access.
WCF-CLIENT: Service endpoint addresses in configuration become CI variables; check each one is reachable from EC2.
WCF-SERVICE: Base addresses and host names in the service configuration change with the new server names.
LS-SMTP-PORT25: AWS throttles outbound port 25 from EC2. Move to port 587 with authentication, or request removal of the limit.
LS-BROADCAST-MULTICAST: UDP broadcast and multicast do not work in an Amazon VPC. The feature needs another discovery method or must be kept off the EC2 move.
LS-IP-ALLOWLIST: An IP allow-list is involved: tell each partner the new AWS Elastic IP, and update our own allow-lists with the new subnets.
LS-CLIENT-IP-LOGIC: Behind an AWS load balancer the application sees the load balancer's IP unless it reads X-Forwarded-For. Without a load balancer there is no change.
LS-STATIC-BIND: A listener is bound to a fixed on-premises IP. Bind to all addresses or use a CI variable for the new IP.
LS-HOSTS-FILE: The code relies on the server's hosts file. Copy the entries to the EC2 host or use Route 53 private records.
LS-LOCALHOST-SERVICE: This calls a service on the same machine. The service must stay on the same EC2 instance.
LS-NETWORK-MOUNT: A network file system is mounted. It must be reachable from EC2 (Amazon FSx / EFS, or the same server over VPN).
LS-LICENSE-SERVER: Licence server or node-locked licence: it may be bound to the old IP, MAC or host name. Ask the vendor for a licence for the new server.
LS-ODBC-DSN: A machine-level ODBC data source (DSN) is used. Create the same DSN on the EC2 host.
LS-CERT-THUMBPRINT: A certificate is selected by thumbprint. Install it in the same store on the EC2 host with its private key, and update the thumbprint if the certificate changes.
LS-LOCAL-DB-FILE: A database file (LocalDB / SQL Compact / .mdf) sits on the server disk. It must be copied with the application and backed up.
CFG-HARDCODED-SECRET: A credential or key is written in source code, so it cannot be replaced by CI. Move it to configuration (a CI variable) and rotate it.
CFG-SECRET-SETTING: A secret is stored in a configuration file. Replace the value with a CI variable supplied from the secret store.
CFG-SECRET-PLACEHOLDER: The secret is already a placeholder filled at deploy time. Add the AWS value to the deployment variables.
CFG-PLAINTEXT-DB-PASSWORD: A database password is in clear text in configuration. Replace it with a CI variable and rotate it.
CFG-LOCAL-DB-PASSWORD: A local development database password in configuration. Keep it out of the AWS configuration.
CFG-DB-PASSWORD-PLACEHOLDER: Database password is a placeholder filled at deploy time. Add the AWS value to the deployment variables.
CFG-PROTECTED-SECTION: The section is encrypted with a key held on the old server (DPAPI or an RSA key container). The new server cannot read it: export and import the key container, or re-encrypt the section from clear text on the new server.
CFG-TRANSFORMS: Per-environment web.config / app.config transforms exist. Add an AWS transform, or use the CI variables from this report.
AUTH-MACHINEKEY: machineKey is configured. Keep the same keys on every server (a CI variable) so existing sessions and tickets stay valid.
WIN-PROTECTEDDATA: Data protected with DPAPI cannot be read on another machine. Find out what is stored this way (files, database values) and re-create it on the new server.
WIN-CNG-CSP: Cryptographic keys live in a machine key container. Export them from the old server (if exportable) and import on the EC2 host.
WIN-CERTSTORE: Certificates are read from the Windows certificate store. Install them (with private keys) on the EC2 host.
WIN-REGISTRY: Registry keys are read or written. Export the listed keys from the old server and import them on the EC2 host, or move the values to configuration.
WIN-REG-FILE: Registry import files (.reg) are shipped with the code. Run them on the EC2 host.
WIN-EVENTLOG: Event log sources are written. Create the source once on the EC2 host (needs administrator rights).
WIN-PERFCOUNTER: Performance counters are used. Register the custom counters on the EC2 host.
WIN-WMI: WMI queries ask the local machine for hardware or OS data. The answers differ on EC2: check what the code does with them.
WIN-COM-INTEROP: A COM component is used. Install and register it on the EC2 host (installer or DLL from the vendor, 32 / 64 bit as today).
WIN-PINVOKE-WIN32: Calls into Windows system DLLs. These exist on Windows EC2; check any call that depends on domain, session or hardware.
WIN-PINVOKE-NATIVE: Calls into native libraries that are not part of Windows. Install the same libraries (same bitness) on the EC2 host.
WIN-SHELL-EXEC: The code starts external programs. Install them at the same path on the EC2 host.
WIN-SERVICE: A Windows service must be installed and started on the EC2 host, with its service account.
WIN-SERVICECONTROLLER: The code controls other Windows services by name. Those services must exist on the same host.
WIN-MSMQ: MSMQ queues are used. Install the MSMQ feature and recreate the queues; messages in flight must be drained before cut-over.
WIN-ACL: File permissions are set or read. Give the application pool / service account the same rights on the EC2 host.
WIN-PROCESS-USER: A process is started as another Windows user. That account must exist on the EC2 host or in the domain.
WIN-NAMED-MMF: Shared memory between processes: the processes must stay on the same EC2 instance.
API-NAMED-SYNC: Named mutexes / events synchronise processes on one machine: the applications involved must stay on the same instance.
WIN-DRIVEINFO: Drives are listed. EBS volumes must give the drive letters the code expects.
WIN-DIRSERVICES: Active Directory is queried. The EC2 hosts must reach a domain controller (extend the domain or use AWS Managed AD).
AUTH-WINDOWS: IIS Windows authentication needs the EC2 host to be joined to the same domain (or a trusted one) with working Kerberos / NTLM.
AUTH-IMPERSONATION: The application impersonates Windows users: the same domain accounts must be reachable from the EC2 host.
AUTH-DEFAULT-CREDENTIALS: Outbound calls use the Windows identity of the process: the service account must be valid on the target systems from AWS.
AUTH-WSFED: Sign-in goes through ADFS / WS-Federation. The relying-party URLs and any IP restrictions at the identity provider must be updated for the new host names.
AUTH-EXTERNAL-IDP: An external identity provider has redirect URLs registered. Update them if the application host names change.
DATA-INTEGRATED-SECURITY: The database login is a Windows account (integrated security). The EC2 host's account must be a valid login on the SQL Server, or the connection string switches to a SQL login.
DATA-ODBC: ODBC drivers are used. Install the same drivers (same bitness) on the EC2 host.
DATA-OLEDB: OLE DB / Jet / ACE providers are used. Install the provider on the EC2 host (Jet is 32-bit only).
DATA-ORACLE-UNMANAGED: The Oracle client is installed on the server. Install the same client and tnsnames on the EC2 host.
DATA-DISTRIBUTED-TX: Distributed transactions (MSDTC) need the transaction coordinator reachable between application and database servers (RPC ports).
DATA-SQLDEPENDENCY: Query notifications need Service Broker enabled on the database.
DB-CROSS-DATABASE: The code uses three-part names between databases: they must stay on the same SQL Server instance (or a linked server replaces them).
DB-LINKED-SERVER: Linked servers point to other servers. They must stay reachable from the new database host.
DB-XP-CMDSHELL: The database runs OS commands or file access. The paths and accounts must exist on the new database host.
DB-BULK-FILE: BULK INSERT reads server-side files. The folder must exist on the new database host.
DB-SQL-AGENT: SQL Server Agent jobs must be moved with the database.
DB-MSDTC: Distributed transactions in T-SQL need the transaction coordinator between database servers.
DB-DATABASE-MAIL: Database Mail uses an SMTP relay that must be reachable from the new database host.
DB-FILESTREAM: FILESTREAM data lives in files next to the database; move them together.
DB-SERVICE-BROKER: Service Broker queues and routes must be recreated or moved with the database.
DB-SERVER-CONFIG: Server-level settings and logins must be recreated on the new database host.
DB-CLR: CLR assemblies are part of the database and move with it; check the CLR setting on the new instance.
DB-FULLTEXT: Full-text catalogues must be rebuilt or moved on the new database host.
TZ-LOCAL-TIME: The code uses the server's local time (DateTime.Now). EC2 Windows runs in UTC by default: set the same time zone as today on each instance, or dates shift.
TZ-SQL-LOCAL-TIME: T-SQL uses the database server's local time (GETDATE). Set the new database host to the same time zone as today.
HV-HARDWARE-ID: Something is bound to a MAC address, BIOS or disk serial number. These change on EC2: find out what depends on them (licences, activation).
HV-MACHINE-NAME: Behaviour depends on the machine name. New servers have new names: use a CI variable or keep the same host names.
HV-LOCAL-DEVICE: Serial / COM / USB devices or dongles are used. They cannot be attached to an EC2 instance: find another way (network device, software licence).
FILE-DRIVE-LETTER: Paths use drive letters. Attach EBS volumes with the same letters, or change the paths in configuration.
FILE-WIN-FOLDERS: Windows special folders (profile, temp, program data) are used. Check the service account's profile on the EC2 host.
FILE-LOCAL-WRITE: The application writes files to the local disk. Size and back up the EBS volume; data on a replaced instance is lost.
IIS-REWRITE: IIS URL Rewrite rules need the URL Rewrite module installed on the EC2 host.
IIS-MODULES-HANDLERS: IIS modules and handlers registered in config must be installed on the EC2 host.
IIS-SESSION-STATE: Session state mode: in-process sessions are lost on restart and break behind a load balancer without sticky sessions. State-server or SQL session addresses are CI variables.
IIS-PUBLISH: Publish profiles point to the old servers. Add the EC2 target to the deployment.
HOST-HTTPSYS-IIS-INPROC: Http.sys / IIS in-process hosting: URL reservations and bindings must be recreated on the EC2 host.
HOST-WINDOWS-SERVICE-LIFETIME: The application runs as a Windows service: install it on the EC2 host.
BG-TASK-SCHEDULER: Windows Task Scheduler tasks must be recreated on the EC2 host with the same triggers and accounts.
BG-HANGFIRE-QUARTZ: A job scheduler runs inside the application. Its store (database) moves with the data; check that jobs do not run twice during a parallel run.
LOG-FILE-TARGETS: Logs are written to files. The log folders must exist on the EC2 host and be collected or rotated.
INT-SMTP-PICKUP-IIS: Mail is dropped in an IIS pickup folder. Install and configure the SMTP service on the EC2 host, or send directly to a relay.
INT-PRINTING: The server prints to printers. Printers must be reachable from AWS (print server over VPN) or printing must change.
INT-FAX: Fax is sent from the server. A fax service or modem is needed on the new host; check whether it is still used.
INT-OFFICE-INTEROP: Microsoft Office is automated on the server. Office must be installed and licensed on the EC2 host.
INT-CRYSTAL: Crystal Reports runtime and licence must be installed on the EC2 host.
INT-SSRS-CLIENT: The SSRS report server address is in configuration (CI variable); the report server must be reachable from EC2.
WEB-REPORTVIEWER: ReportViewer points to a report server; the address is a CI variable.
INT-SHAREPOINT-EXCHANGE: SharePoint object model or Exchange Web Services is used: the target servers and URLs must stay reachable from AWS.
BUILD-GAC-REFERENCE: An assembly is loaded from the Global Assembly Cache. Install it into the GAC of the EC2 host.
BUILD-INSTALLER: An installer project exists. Use it for the EC2 deployment or keep the manual steps as a checklist.
BUILD-PRIVATE-FEED: A private NuGet feed is used by builds. Build agents must still reach it; EC2 hosts do not need it.
